svg.title: Main trans-Saharan trade routes
svg.desc: Map of North and West Africa with three main trans-Saharan routes: a western route from Sijilmasa through the salt mines of Taghaza to Walata and Timbuktu; a central route from Tunis and Ghadames through Agadez to Gao and Kano; and an eastern route from Tripoli through the Fezzan and Bilma to Kanem and Lake Chad. Gold, kola nuts, ivory and slaves went north; salt, horses, cloth, copper, books and luxury goods came south.
svg.text: S A H A R A
Going north: gold, kola nuts, ivory, slaves, leather
Going south: salt, horses, cloth, copper, books,
Camels carried goods across the desert.
